name: Vilazodone Hydrochloride
meta: Serotonin partial agonist and reuptake inhibitor (SPARI)
sections: Serotonin partial agonist and reuptake inhibitor (SPARI)

Approved in the USA in 2011 and Canada in 2018 as a combined SSRI and 5-HT1A partial agonist (SPARI). First approval/introduction: US FDA 2011 (developed by Merck KGaA; licensed to Clinical Data / Forest Laboratories).

Inhibits serotonin reuptake and acts as a partial agonist at 5-HT1A receptors, which may accelerate desensitisation of autoreceptors. Receptor / target profile: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor (Ki 0.1 nM) and 5-HT1A partial agonist (intrinsic activity ~60–70%); negligible affinity for other monoamine transporters.
Summary: Bioavailability ~72% when taken with food (must be taken with food). Tmax 4–5 h. ~96–99% protein bound. Metabolised mainly by CYP3A4. Half-life ~25 h.
Start 10 mg once daily for 7 days, then 20 mg once daily
May increase to 40 mg once daily after at least 7 days
Must be taken with food (absorption halves when fasting)
With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors: max 20 mg/day
Taper (e.g. 40 → 20 mg for 4 days, then 10 mg for 3 days) when stopping
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
No adjustment for mild–moderate; not studied in severe.
Not approved (not effective in paediatric trials).
Data limited; weigh risks and benefits.
Use with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitors
Sexual dysfunction (lower rates than many SSRIs)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) – reduce dose to 20 mg
Strong CYP3A4 inducers – consider dose increase
Must be taken with food; avoid alcohol and grapefruit.
Serotonin syndrome, lethargy, restlessness, hallucinations. Supportive care.
Rickels et al., J Clin Psychiatry 2009 and Khan et al., 2011 – 8-week placebo-controlled trials demonstrated efficacy at 40 mg/day in MDD.
Diarrhoea and nausea are common initially
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
